findings.claim: The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. When no SurrogateType is set, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type) and never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key] or [IgnoreMember] on T. A member marked [IgnoreMember] on T is therefore serialized, and integer [Key]s are replaced by name-sorted string keys. The requirement also implies [DataContract]/[DataMember] on T should be honoured, which is the case a dependency-free Project A can actually use, and that is ignored too. Ledger L21 says to follow the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests: MessagePackObjectOnReferencedType_IgnoreMemberIsHonoured and DataContractOnReferencedType_NonDataMemberIsNotSerialized. Both assert the generated MyTypeFormatter source never mentions 'Secret'. Both fail on head because contractless mode includes every public read-write member.

findings.claim: An unrelated security regression is bundled into this feature. MessagePackSecurity's fallback for key types without a hash-collision-resistant comparer now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing TypeAccessException. In UntrustedData mode, dictionaries and hash sets keyed by arbitrary types then use non-resistant hashing, which reopens hash-flooding DoS. The requirement asks for nothing like this, and it contradicts the secure-by-default history recorded in L12.

receipt_plan.detail: Call MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.GetEqualityComparer<SomeCustomStruct>() for a user-defined struct. On base it throws TypeAccessException; on head it returns EqualityComparer<SomeCustomStruct>.Default. Alternatively, deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKey,int> with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData) and observe that no exception is thrown on head.
